Tobijah
to-BYE-jah
n. (proper, a Levite teacher; also one of the crowned men of Zechariah 6)
Hebrew Towbiyah, from towb, good, and Yah — Jehovah is good. Two men bear it: a Levite whom Jehoshaphat sent through Judah to teach, and one of the exiles whose gift furnished the crowns of Zechariah's great sign.

Biblical Definition

Jehoshaphat sent a teaching commission through every city of Judah with the book of the law: “And with them he sent Levites, even Shemaiah, and Nethaniah, and Zebadiah, and Asahel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehonathan, and Adonijah, and Tobijah, and Tobadonijah, Levites” (2 Chronicles 17:8). The other Tobijah appears in one of the most remarkable acted prophecies in Scripture. Zechariah is told: “Take of them of the captivity, even of Heldai, of Tobijah, and of Jedaiah, which are come from Babylon, and come thou the same day, and go into the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah” (Zechariah 6:10), and from their silver and gold to make crowns and set them on the head of Joshua the high priest, and to say, Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH, who shall build the temple of the LORD, and shall be a priest upon his throne. Then: “And the crowns shall be to Helem, and to Tobijah, and to Jedaiah... for a memorial in the temple of the LORD” (Zechariah 6:14).

Origin & Era

Webster (1828) has no entry for this proper name; Scripture fixes it as one of the Levites Jehoshaphat sent to teach in Judah, and as one of the returned exiles whose gift made Zechariah's crowns.

expand to see more

CROWN, n. An ornament worn on the head by kings and sovereign princes, as a badge of imperial or regal power.

BRANCH, n. In Scripture, a title of the Messiah, the shoot out of the stem of Jesse.

MEMORIAL, n. That which preserves the memory of something; anything that serves to keep in memory.

CATECHIZE, v.t. To instruct by asking questions and receiving answers, and offering explanations and corrections.

TYPE, n. In theology, a figure or representation of something to come; a prefiguration.

Key Scripture

2 Chronicles 17:8 — "And with them he sent Levites, even Shemaiah, and Nethaniah, and Zebadiah, and Asahel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehonathan, and Adonijah, and Tobijah, and Tobadonijah, Levites; and with them Elishama and Jehoram, priests."

Zechariah 6:10 — "Take of them of the captivity, even of Heldai, of Tobijah, and of Jedaiah, which are come from Babylon, and come thou the same day, and go into the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah;"

Zechariah 6:14 — "And the crowns shall be to Helem, and to Tobijah, and to Jedaiah, and to Hen the son of Zephaniah, for a memorial in the temple of the LORD."

Zechariah 6:13 — "Even he shall build the temple of the LORD; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both."

Modern Corruption

The offices of priest and king are kept apart in Israel by law and united only in one man; Zechariah's crowns on a priest's head are the sign of it, and the chapter is often read as anything but that.

expand to see more

Under the law the two offices were rigorously separate, and Uzziah was struck with leprosy for crossing the line. Zechariah 6 deliberately crosses it under God's own instruction: crowns made from exiles' gold, set on the head of Joshua the high priest, with the declaration Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH... he shall build the temple of the LORD; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both. No mere high priest could be that. The sign points past Joshua to the one who is both, and Hebrews takes it up in the priesthood after the order of Melchizedek.

The homely detail is that the crowns were funded by three men just back from Babylon — Heldai, Tobijah and Jedaiah — and afterwards hung in the temple as a memorial to them. The other Tobijah spent his life going from town to town in Judah with the book of the law, teaching. A name that means Jehovah is good is attached to a man who taught the law and to a man whose silver became a sign of the Priest-King. Neither man did anything spectacular; both are in the Bible because of what they gave to the work of God.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Towbiyah (H2900), Jehovah is good; towb (H2896), good; atarah (H5850), a crown; tsemach (H6780), the Branch.

expand to see more

Hebrew Towbiyah (H2900) — Tobijah; Jehovah is good.

Hebrew towb (H2896) — good; the element in the name.

Hebrew atarah (H5850) — a crown; made of the exiles' silver and gold.

Hebrew tsemach (H6780) — a sprout, the Branch; the title given in Zechariah 6:12.

Hebrew zikkarown (H2146) — a memorial; the crowns kept in the temple.

Usage

"“He sent Levites... and Tobijah” — teaching through every city of Judah."

"“Take of them of the captivity, even of Heldai, of Tobijah” — the gold."

"“He shall be a priest upon his throne” — what the crowns signified."
